description: The rows this document holds of one declared format. Ask `formats` first for the column names — they belong to the document. `match` filters on exact values (text and enum members case-insensitively; a list column, the rows holding the one named), `search` a substring in every column as shown (a price as 12.90, a link by its row’s name) but yes/no, and `order` sorts by any column, computed too — by default the one a row is named by, which is its first text column. Narrow `columns` to get a table of just those — a computed column (a total, or one worked out from the row) by its name too; leave it out and each row comes back in full with its empty columns left out, **and with what its claims say about it** — proved, failed, or unchecked when the row has nothing in a column one of them names. Every row carries the id the other tools use to correct or remove it. Reads the file; never modifies it.

columns.description: Column names to show, as a table — stored or computed. Omit for every column.

descending.description: Sort the other way. Defaults to false.

format.description: The declared format, by name. `formats` lists them.

limit.description: Rows to return. Defaults to 25, at most 200.

match.description: Column name to the value it must equal. Text and enum columns match without regard to case; money or a quantity, a range: `10..50 ILS`. A list is any of them (`[planned, in_progress]`; a list column holding any), `{not: x}` or `{not: [a, b]}` none (empty passes), `null` empty. A date takes `today`, `yesterday`, `tomorrow`, `before|after today`, `within|last 14 days`, `this|last|next week|month|year`.

offset.description: Rows to skip first — the `offset` a cut-short answer hands back for the rest.

order.description: A declared column to sort by. Defaults to the column a row is named by — its first text column — which is what the screen sorts by too. Ordering by the generated id shuffles, since an id is generated rather than counted.

path.description: Absolute path to a .emd file on this machine.

search.description: A substring, in every column as shown but yes/no.

values.description: A column: each value it holds and how many rows, under the other filters.

view.description: A saved view’s name: its match, search, order and columns, under any given here.

name: format_rows
title: Rows of a declared format
